content:
World of Warcraft Forever has now been out for a couple of weeks, and it's had a remarkably smooth launch. But now that players are starting to level up enough to engage with dungeons, Blizzard is trying to nail down exactly how dungeons should reward players.

Over the weekend, Blizzard pushed out a November 13 hotfix that made it so if there's any player in a group that's too high of a level to earn experience from monsters, no one in that group gets experience. The goal seems to be to get rid of boosting, where one high-level player can carry a group of players through dungeons to level them up quickly. But that solution backfired.

The problem is that in a lot of Forever's dungeons, there's a wide level range, so players on the high end of that range ended up accidentally nullifying everyone else's experience in the dungeon. That even happened to me on Saturday when trying to run Excavation Site with a level 37 player in my group.

The next day, Blizzard admitted that hotfix went too far. On the WoW Forever forums, community manager Kaivax posted, saying, "Yesterday, we updated dungeon play so that experience granted by an enemy in an instance is nullified if a high level player is in the group and enemy is trivial to that player. For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon."

Instead, Blizzard changed the way the restriction works. Rather than basing it on whether or not an enemy is "trivial" to any of the players, there's now a flat level difference restriction on experience. As Kaivax puts it, "We’ve just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so that the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies."

For those who are just trying to do dungeons as they naturally come up while questing, the latest update should completely fix the issue, while also preventing boosters from powering people through the game. After all, Blizzard is dead-set on encouraging players to level out in the world, and is apparently not afraid of using some heavy-handed tactics to do so.

This also isn’t the first time that Blizzard has needed to adjust dungeon experience. Back when the WoW Forever beta first opened, the company severely limited the amount of XP you get from dungeons, only to buff it last week – even if it’s still far below what you’d earn in Classic. Blizzard has also changed the way gold is earned, in order to stop people from feeling like they had to hoard quest turn-ins for when they hit max level.
